To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the higher education system is complex and changing and that the governance of this system is complex and contested.
higher education is a complex, multifaceted, and highly dynamic system, and that the governance of higher education is a central element in the analysis of the evolution of these systems.

1) the higher education governance arrangements in the 14 nations examined in this volume are complex, and 2) the complexity of these systems is a function of their size, their history, and their political, cultural and institutional context.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how decisions about higher education are made and how those decisions affect the nature and structure of higher education systems.
the nature of the relationships among the various levels of the system and the nature of the interactions between the various bodies or groups that operate at these different levels.
understanding the processes by which higher education systems and institutions are governed, and the consequences of these processes on the nature and quality of higher education.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the contributors to this collection have sought to understand the governance of higher education as a complex process of decision-making that is shaped by the interaction of multiple actors operating at different levels within higher education systems.
higher education is governed by a complex and dynamic interaction of bodies, groups and individuals operating at different levels and in different contexts.

the governance of higher education is a complex process of interaction among multiple stakeholders, both within and outside the system, and the outcomes of these interactions vary across time, place and context.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
governance is the process through which the various actors in higher education determine what it is and what it should be.

governance in higher education is the dynamic interaction of bodies, groups, and institutions at multiple levels of a higher system, which determines what higher education is in a particular place at a particular point in time.
governance is the process by which decisions are made and implemented at different levels of higher education systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
governance is not just a matter of who is in charge, or who makes the decisions.
governance is a dynamic process and the way in which higher education is governed will change as new actors enter the system and as new issues emerge.
the nature of the governance of higher education is complex and that there is no single model of higher education governance.
